newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher on lack of hedging.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher on lack of hedging.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended higher on a lack of hedge-related selling because of the weekend snowfall in the upper Midwest, traders said.
The winter weather across key spring wheat growing areas brought movement of wheat to a virtual standstill.
"Nothing moved in the country this weekend, and our market showed that," a MGE trader said. "It was one of the slowest days I've ever seen."
MGE spring wheat closed two to 11-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with Dec up 11-1/2 cents at $4.27. March settled up four cents at $3.89.
U.S. wheat markets also drew support from worries over possible cold damage to U.S. hard red winter wheat, and from concern over the extent of damage from last week's storms in southern Argentina.
LFG sold one million March bushels and Country Hedging sold 500,000 March. Benson-Quinn bought 800,000 March. CIS bought 500,000 March and May bushels.
MGE barley futures did not trade and settled unchanged.
